newsitem.title: USA: NYS might end FY 1997 with $1 bln surplus - paper.
newsitem.headline: NYS might end FY 1997 with $1 bln surplus - paper.

text.p: New York State, which faces a structural deficit of $2 billion to $3 billion in fiscal 1998, might end the 1997 fiscal year with a surplus of as much as $1 billion, the Albany Times Union said on Wednesday.
The paper said that Gov George Pataki might announce the surplus as soon as early this afternoon, when he makes his State of the State address.

Pataki also is expected to announce a multi-year plan to help keep local property taxes from rising by providing more funds for school districts that agree to keep their property taxes flat, according to newspaper reports.
But a reduction in utility taxes no longer is anticipated as it would be too expensive, the Times Union said.
And the New York Post, in its Wednesday edition, said Pataki is expected to propose doubling the $110 million a year the state spends on school textbooks.
